newsitem.title: USA: U.S. refiners flirting with foreign crudes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. refiners flirting with foreign crudes.

text.p: U.S. refiners flirted with foreign crudes Tuesday as they pondered the regional impact of impending Iraqi exports, traders said.
The spread between January West Texas Intermediate and North Sea Brent hovered around $1.05-15 a barrel.
The increasing appeal of Brent on the Gulf Coast was reflected in the declining differential of Light Louisiana Sweet grade.
LLS sank to WTI/Cushing plus 78-85 cents a barrel, down from 89-91 cents on Monday.
"LLS has come off pretty considerably, so has dated Brent," one trader said. "Maybe Brent could be offered (into the U.S.) at WTI plus 25-30 cents for January delivered."
A Wall Street trader was heard to have several Brent cargoes, and possibly sold two or three to a Gulf Coast refiner, although the transaction could not be confirmed.
Meanwhile, some Iraqi crude is poised to reach U.S. refiners on the Gulf Coast and in the Caribbean, putting additional pressure on domestic sour grades and regional Venezuelan and Mexican crudes.
Among likely U.S. buyers are Coastal Coastal and Mobil, industry sources said.
U.S. firms could begin lifting Iraqi crude in January, the sources said.
Brazil's state oil company Petrobras is expected to buy around 25,000 barrels per day, possibly displacing West African crudes, traders said.
The Brazilians bought a peak of 160,000 bpd of Iraqi Kirkuk and Basrah Light crudes before Iraq invaded Kuwait in 1990.
Petrobras is still awaiting a price formula tied to either WTI or Dated Brent before it can sign a deal, traders said.

In regional spot activity, Colombia's state owned oil company Ecopetrol sold at least one cargo of Vasconia for mid-January to a Gulf Coast refiner. The refiner is reoffering the crude at February WTI minus $1.85 a barrel fob, trade sources said.
Ecopetrol also sold Cano Limon and South Blend cargoes for end-January to Spain's Repsol for the La Pampilla refinery in Peru, the sources added.
The Cano Limon was sold at around Feb WTI minus $1.35-45 a barrel, while the South Blend went for around Feb WTI minus $2.15 a barrel.
Finally, Ecopetrol was heard to have sold a cargo of Cusiana to state owned Petroleos de Venezuela unit Maraven at around Feb WTI plus 45 cents, traders said.
Separately, British Petroleum sold a Cusiana cargo for loading December 30-31 into the Gulf Coast at Feb WTI plus 47 cents.
Meanwhile, Shell sold Vasconia for January 5-9 to a Gulf Coast refiner in a confidential trasncation.
In the U.S. aftermarket, paper February Brent partial cargoes changed hands at $22.85, $22.88 and $22.90 a barrel, five to 10 cents higher than the IPE settlement.
Intermonth spreads were also stronger. Jan/Feb Brent traded at 52/53/55 cents, up seven to 10 cents from the London close.
--Patricia Garip-Bertuol NY Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
